mainTopic: Hidden forms of רבית: a lender's free benefits, taking back interest paid in goods, and charging more for later payment
overview: This amud opens by finishing a story about רב יוסף בר חמא, who used his debtors' slaves for free. His son רבא shows him that when the slave's owner owes you money, this looks like רבית, and he takes back his practice. Next, אביי and רבא argue about how a court takes back interest that was paid in goods: wheat given at a discount, and a cloak. רבא adds a case where interest was paid through an overpriced rental, and the lender is held to the price he agreed to. Then a new משנה teaches that a higher price for paying later is allowed for rent but forbidden for a sale. The גמרא explains why: rent is only owed at the end, based on a פסוק, so the higher rent is the real price, while a sale price is owed right away. Finally, רב נחמן allows טרשא, a quiet higher price for later payment. רב פפא and רב חמא each explain why their own טרשא deals are allowed.

steps.title: The reason the master doesn't mind
steps.stepSummary: The last words of the ruling רב יוסף בר חמא relied on: the master is happy that his slave doesn't get lazy.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the master is pleased that his slave doesn't lose his work habits.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the reason behind the ruling רב יוסף בר חמא was relying on. Someone who makes another person's slave work doesn't owe pay, because the master is glad his slave stays busy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that the owner gets something out of this: his slave stays used to working. So taking the slave's work is not treated as taking something of value. This is the claim that רבא will challenge next.

keyTerms.meaning: it is pleasing / acceptable to him
become undone, here meaning to get lazy or lose work habits

phrases.english: for it is pleasing to him (the master)
that his slave not become undone (idle).

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּנִיחָא לֵיהּ דְּלָא נִסְתְּרֵי עַבְדֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the reason, begun earlier on the daf, for why using a slave's work is free.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A slave's owner is glad when his slave keeps working, so using the slave does not create a debt for wages.

steps.title: רבא: when you are owed money, it looks like interest
steps.stepSummary: רבא tells his father that the ruling only applies when the master owes you nothing. A lender using his debtor's slave looks like he is collecting רבית.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: That rule applies only when the one who uses the slave is not owed money by the master. But you, Master, are owed money by them, so it looks like interest.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges his father's practice. He limits the ruling to a case where there is no loan between the two people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא does not argue with the ruling itself. He says it doesn't fit this case. When there is a loan, the free work the lender gets looks like a payment for waiting on the loan, and that is a kind of רבית.

keyTerms.meaning: he is owed money by him

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying the slave rule is wrong. He is only saying it doesn't apply when the slave's owner is your borrower.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is רבא, the son of רב יוסף בר חמא, speaking to his father.

phrases.english: These words apply where
he is not owed money by him.
But you, Master, since you are owed money by them,
it looks like interest.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָנֵי מִילֵּי הֵיכָא דְּלָא מַסֵּיק בֵּיהּ זוּזֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the ruling from step 1 so that it doesn't cover a lender and his borrower.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף בר חמא's practice of using his debtors' slaves
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The 'master doesn't mind' reason works only when there is no loan. With a loan, the free use of the slave looks like a reward for lending.

steps.title: Proof from רב נחמן about living in a borrower's courtyard
steps.stepSummary: Normally someone who lives in another person's courtyard without permission doesn't pay rent. But a lender who lives in his borrower's courtyard must pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב יוסף בר מניומי said in the name of רב נחמן: Even though the חכמים said that someone who lives in his friend's courtyard without his knowledge doesn't have to pay him rent, if he lent him money and then lives in his courtyard, he must pay him rent.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא backs up his point with a ruling of רב נחמן. That ruling follows exactly the same pattern as the slave case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually free use of an empty courtyard costs the owner nothing, so no rent is owed. Once there is a loan, the same free use looks like a benefit the lender gets for his loan, so he must pay. The slave works the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: one who lives in his friend's courtyard

phrases.english: As רב יוסף בר מניומי said
that רב נחמן said:
Even though they said
one who lives in his friend's courtyard without his knowledge
does not need to pay him rent.
If he lent him money and then lives in his courtyard,
he must pay him rent.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף בַּר מִנְיוֹמֵי אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives support for רבא's challenge in step 2.
steps.raayaObject: That a loan turns otherwise free use into something that looks like רבית
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב נחמן's ruling about a lender living in his borrower's courtyard
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets a general rule. Free use that would normally be allowed becomes a problem of looking like רבית once there is a loan between the people.

steps.title: רב יוסף בר חמא takes back his practice
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף בר חמא accepts his son's argument and stops using his debtors' slaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I take it back.
steps.whatsHappening: The father agrees with רבא and drops his practice, so this part of the sugya ends here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling about using someone's slave for free stays in place. Its use is limited, though: it does not apply between a lender and his borrower.

keyTerms.meaning: I retract / I take it back

steps.whatToRemember: A lender may not use his borrower's slave (or courtyard) for free, even where a stranger could, because it looks like רבית.

phrases.english: He said to him: I take it back.
phrases.notes: Now רב יוסף בר חמא is answering his son.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הֲדַרִי בִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge and proof from steps 2 and 3.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Using a borrower's slave without paying is forbidden as looking like רבית.

steps.title: אביי: interest paid in wheat at a discount
steps.stepSummary: Wheat sells at 4 measures per זוז, but the borrower pays a זוז of interest with 5 measures. אביי says the court takes back only 4, because the extra one was just a discount.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Someone is owed money as interest by his friend. Wheat is selling in the market at four measures for a זוז, and the borrower gives him five. When we take it back from the lender, we take back four. The other one is just a discount the borrower gave him.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. אביי rules on how much a court takes back when interest was paid in wheat worth more than the debt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For אביי, the interest owed was one זוז, which equals 4 measures. The fifth measure was not interest. It was like a friendly discount in a sale, so the lender keeps it.

keyTerms.meaning: measures (of wheat), a unit of volume
we (the court) take it out of his hands
giving a discount / lowering the price

phrases.english: אביי said:

phrases.aramaic: הַאי מַאן דְּמַסֵּיק זוּזֵי דְרִיבִּיתָא בְּחַבְרֵיהּ
phrases.english: This one who is owed money of interest by his friend,
and wheat is going
at four measures per זוז in the market,
and he (the borrower) gives him five,
when we take it out from him (the lender),
we take out four from him.
The other one is a discount
that he gave him as a lower price.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הַאי מַאן דְּמַסֵּיק זוּזֵי דְרִיבִּיתָא בְּחַבְרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about taking back interest that was paid in goods.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only the market value of the interest owed (4 measures) is taken back. The extra measure counts as a discount.

steps.title: רבא: take back all five
steps.stepSummary: רבא disagrees: all five measures came to the lender as interest, so all five are taken back.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: We take five from him, because from the start it came into his hands as interest.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא argues with אביי about the wheat case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי looks at how much interest was owed. רבא looks at why the wheat was handed over. Since the whole payment was given as interest, none of it counts as a gift or a discount.

keyTerms.meaning: as interest, in the role of interest

phrases.english: רבא said:
We take out five from him,
since from the start, as interest,
it came into his hands.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: חַמְשָׁה מַפְּקִינַן מִינֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with אביי's ruling in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everything paid as interest is taken back, including the 'extra' measure.

steps.title: אביי: interest paid with a cloak
steps.stepSummary: A borrower owes 4 זוזים of interest and pays with a cloak. אביי says the court takes back the 4 זוזים, not the cloak itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אביי said: Someone is owed four זוזים of interest by his friend, and the borrower gives him a cloak for them. When we take it back from the lender, we take back four זוזים. We do not take the cloak from him.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a second ruling about interest paid with an object instead of money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For אביי, what the lender wrongly took was money, 4 זוזים. The cloak was like a separate sale used to settle that money. So the court makes him return the money's worth, and he keeps the cloak.

keyTerms.meaning: in place of them / for them

phrases.english: And אביי said:

phrases.aramaic: הַאי מַאן דְּמַסֵּיק אַרְבְּעָה זוּזֵי דְרִיבִּיתָא בְּחַבְרֵיהּ
phrases.english: This one who is owed four זוזים of interest by his friend,
and he gives him a cloak in place of them,
when we take it out from him,
we take out four (זוזים) from him;
the cloak we do not take out from him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הַאי מַאן דְּמַסֵּיק אַרְבְּעָה זוּזֵי דְרִיבִּיתָא בְּחַבְרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second ruling by אביי on the same theme of interest paid in goods.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The lender returns the money value of the interest, and the cloak itself stays with him.

steps.title: רבא: take back the cloak itself
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that the court takes the actual cloak away from the lender.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: We take the cloak from him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא disagrees with אביי again, this time about the cloak. His reason comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the argument is not about how much is returned. It is about what is returned: the object itself or its money value.

phrases.english: רבא said:
We take the cloak out from him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: גְּלִימָא מַפְּקִינַן מִינֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with אביי's ruling in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The cloak given as interest is itself taken back.

steps.title: Why רבא takes the cloak: so people won't talk
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains רבא's reason: otherwise people will point at the lender's cloak and say it is a cloak of interest.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? So that people won't say: the cloak he is wearing is a cloak of interest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for רבא's reason and gives it. The cloak must go back so that people won't see the lender wearing something he got as interest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's reason is about how things look in public, not about the amount of money. Paying back 4 זוזים would fix the money side, but the lender would still be seen wearing a cloak that people would call an 'interest cloak'.

keyTerms.meaning: so that they should not say
that he is wearing (literally, covering himself and standing)

steps.whatToRemember: אביי and רבא argue twice about interest paid in goods. אביי returns only the money value of the interest owed. רבא returns everything that was given as interest, and returns the actual object so that it won't be seen as an 'interest cloak'.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
So that they should not say:
"The cloak that he is wearing
is a cloak of interest."

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא, כִּי הֵיכִי דְּלָא לֵימְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason for רבא's ruling in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבא requires returning the cloak itself and not just its value
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: To prevent people from saying the lender is wearing a cloak that came from interest

steps.title: Interest paid through an overpriced courtyard rental
steps.stepSummary: רבא: if a lender rented a courtyard worth ten for twelve, using the twelve זוזים of interest to cover the rent, the court takes back twelve.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Someone is owed twelve זוזים of interest by his fellow. He rents from him a courtyard that normally rents for ten, but they set the price at twelve. When the court takes the interest back from the lender, it takes twelve.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives another case of returning interest. This time the interest was paid by letting the lender use a courtyard instead of paying rent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The courtyard's normal rent is only ten, but they agreed on twelve, the exact amount of the interest. רבא says the court goes by the agreed price, so the lender must return all twelve, not just the courtyard's market value of ten.

phrases.english: Rava said:
This one who is owed twelve zuz
of interest by his fellow,
and he rented a courtyard from him
that normally rents for ten,
but he rented it to him for twelve.
phrases.notes: The borrower lets the lender off the rent, and that is how the twelve זוזים of interest get paid.

phrases.english: When we take it back from him,
we take twelve back from him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הַאי מַאן דְּמַסֵּיק תְּרֵיסַר זוּזֵי דְּרִיבִּיתָא בְּחַבְרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new case from רבא about returning interest paid in a non-cash form, continuing the theme of steps 5-9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Interest paid through an inflated rental price is returned at the full agreed price (twelve), not the market value (ten).

steps.title: Why can't the lender claim the normal price?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא מדפתי asks רבינא: let the lender say he only agreed to twelve because he wasn't really paying, so now he should owe the usual ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא מדפתי said to רבינא: Let the lender say, 'When I rented it at that price, it was because I was getting it for free. Now that I'm not, I'll pay what everyone else pays.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא challenges רבא's ruling by giving the lender a reasonable-sounding argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lender claims the price of twelve was never a real price, since nothing actually changed hands. If the deal now becomes a real rental, he wants to pay the normal ten, which would mean returning only ten.

keyTerms.meaning: I was profiting / gaining from it

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא מִדִּפְתִּי לְרָבִינָא:
phrases.english: Rav Acha of Difti said to Ravina:
But let him say to him:
When I rented it at this price,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the corrected wording is the word in square brackets, 'I rented.'

phrases.english: it was because I was profiting from it;
now that I am not profiting from it,
the way everyone rents
is how I rent.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא מִדִּפְתִּי לְרָבִינָא: וְלֵימָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's ruling in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that twelve is taken back
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The twelve price was only agreed because no money really changed hands; the lender should be able to claim the market price of ten.

steps.title: You agreed to the price
steps.stepSummary: The lender's claim is rejected: he knowingly agreed to twelve, so he is held to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because we say to him: You thought it over and accepted it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב אחא's challenge and defends רבא's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lender chose to rent at twelve with his eyes open. He cannot now go back on the price he agreed to, so the court values the rental at twelve and he returns twelve.

keyTerms.meaning: You considered and accepted (you agreed knowingly)

steps.whatToRemember: Interest paid through a rental is returned at the price the lender agreed to, because he knowingly accepted it.

phrases.english: Because he says to him:
phrases.notes: The court (or the borrower) answers the lender like this.

phrases.english: You considered it and accepted it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דַּאֲמַר לֵיהּ: סְבַרְתְּ וְקַבֵּלְתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the claim by pointing to the lender's own consent
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The lender can fall back on the market price because the twelve was not a real payment.
steps.terutzMaskana: He knowingly agreed to twelve, so he is bound to it and twelve is returned.

steps.title: Charging more for later payment: rent yes, sale no
steps.stepSummary: The משנה allows a higher rent for paying monthly but forbids a higher sale price for paying later.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may raise the price for rent, but not for a sale. How? Someone rents out his courtyard and says: 'If you pay now, it's ten סלעים a year; if you pay monthly, it's a סלע a month (twelve a year).' This is allowed. Someone sells his field and says: 'If you pay now, it's a thousand זוז; if you pay at harvest time, it's twelve מנה (1,200 זוז).' This is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens. It sets two cases side by side: higher price for later payment is fine with rent but forbidden with a sale.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both cases the extra money is linked to waiting for payment, which looks like interest. Yet the משנה permits it for rent and forbids it for a sale, which sets up the גמרא's question about the difference.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
One may increase the price of rent
but one may not increase the price of a sale.
How so? He rented his courtyard to him

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר לוֹ: ״אִם מֵעַכְשָׁיו אַתָּה נוֹתֵן לִי –
phrases.english: and said to him: 'If you pay me now,

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי הוּא לְךָ בְּעֶשֶׂר סְלָעִים לַשָּׁנָה,
phrases.english: it is yours for ten sela a year;
but if you pay month by month,
it is a sela per month.' This is permitted.
He sold his field to him

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר לוֹ: ״אִם מֵעַכְשָׁיו אַתָּה נוֹתֵן לִי –
phrases.english: and said to him: 'If you pay me now,
it is yours for a thousand zuz;

phrases.aramaic: אִם לַגּוֹרֶן – בִּשְׁנֵים עָשָׂר מָנֶה״, אָסוּר.
phrases.english: if at harvest time, for twelve maneh.' This is forbidden.
phrases.notes: Twelve מנה is 1,200 זוז, so waiting costs two hundred more.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַרְבִּין עַל הַשָּׂכָר וְאֵין מַרְבִּין עַל הַמֶּכֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה; a fresh topic within the laws of רבית.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A higher price for later payment is permitted for rent but forbidden for a sale.

steps.title: Why is rent different from a sale?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the difference is between the first case (rent) and the second case (sale).
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about the first case, and what is different about the second case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the משנה treats the two cases differently. This sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both cases the person who pays later pays more, so both seem like paying for waiting. The גמרא wants to know what makes rent permitted and a sale forbidden.

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is different about the first clause
and what is different about the last clause?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא רֵישָׁא וּמַאי שְׁנָא סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the distinction made in the משנה of step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason rent may be priced higher for later payment while a sale may not.

steps.title: Rent is only due at the end, so paying early is a discount
steps.stepSummary: רבה and רב יוסף: rent is only owed at the end, so the higher price is the real price and paying early just earns a discount.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה and רב יוסף both say: Rent is only owed at the end. Since the time to collect it has not yet come, the extra is not payment for waiting. The higher price is simply what it is worth, and when he says 'If you pay now it's ten סלעים a year,' he is just giving him a discount.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה and רב יוסף answer the question of step 14 and explain why the rent case is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since rent is not owed until the end of the rental, paying month by month is not 'late,' so the twelve is the real price and not a charge for waiting. The ten is a discount for paying before the money is owed. With a sale, the money is owed right away, so the extra for paying at harvest is a charge for waiting, which is interest.

keyTerms.meaning: Rent is only due at the end
Payment for waiting (a form of interest)

steps.whatToRemember: Rent is owed only at the end, so a higher monthly price is the real price and paying up front just earns a discount. That is why it is not interest.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the renter is paying extra for waiting. The twelve is the normal price; the ten is a discount for paying early, before the rent is even owed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the key test for these cases: extra money counts as interest only if it is paid for waiting on money that is already owed.

phrases.english: Rabbah and Rav Yosef both say:
Rent is only owed at the end,

phrases.aramaic: וְהַאי כֵּיוָן דְּלָא מְטָא זִמְנֵיהּ לְמִיגְבֵּא –
phrases.english: and in this case, since its time to be collected has not arrived,
it is not payment for waiting for him.
Rather, it is its value, because that is what it is worth,
phrases.notes: He means the higher price, twelve, is the courtyard's real rental value.

phrases.english: and what he says to him,
'If you pay me now,

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי הוּא לְךָ בְּעֶשֶׂר סְלָעִים לְשָׁנָה״ –
phrases.english: it is yours for ten sela a year,'
is just a discount that he is giving him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה וְרַב יוֹסֵף דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ: שְׂכִירוּת אֵינָהּ מִשְׁתַּלֶּמֶת אֶלָּא בַּסּוֹף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Since rent is only due at the end, the higher monthly price is the true value and the lower up-front price is a discount, not payment for waiting.

steps.title: Why a higher price for paying later on a sale is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רבה and רב יוסף finish their answer: in a sale, the money is owed right away, so charging more for waiting is payment for waiting, and that is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the second case, since it is a sale and the seller is owed the money now, the extra charge is payment for waiting, and that is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second half of רבה and רב יוסף's answer, now explaining the sale case in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With rent, the higher price is the real price, because rent is only due at the end. With a sale, the money is due the moment the sale happens. So any extra charge for paying later is payment for the seller's waiting, which is רבית.

keyTerms.meaning: The later part of the משנה
Payment for waiting, a form of רבית

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a key rule. When a payment is already due, any extra charge for delaying it counts as רבית.

phrases.english: The latter clause: since it is a sale,
and he is supposed to take the money from now,

phrases.aramaic: הִלְכָּךְ אֲגַר נְטַר לֵיהּ הוּא, וְאָסוּר.
phrases.english: therefore it is payment for waiting for him, and it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: סֵיפָא: כֵּיוָן דִּזְבִינֵי נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-part answer begun in step 15
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the difference between the rent case and the sale case?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A sale price is owed immediately, so charging extra for delay is payment for waiting and is forbidden.

steps.title: The פסוק showing rent is paid at the end
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the חכמים based the rent rule on the פסוק 'like a hired worker year by year': rent for this year is only paid in the next year.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: the חכמים looked closely at this and based it on the פסוק 'like a hired worker year by year'. This year's rent is only paid in the following year.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a פסוק as the source for the idea that rent is only owed at the end of the rental period.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole difference between rent and sale depends on rent not being due until the end. רבא shows this is not just logic. It comes from a פסוק about a hired worker, whose wages for one year are paid only afterward.

keyTerms.meaning: They based it on a פסוק

phrases.english: Rava said: The Sages looked closely
at this matter and based it on a verse:
"Like a hired worker, year by year"
the rent of this year
is only paid in the next year.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: דָּקוּ בַּהּ רַבָּנַן בְּהָא מִילְּתָא וְאוֹקְמוּהָ אַקְּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies a פסוק supporting the principle used in steps 15-16
steps.raayaObject: Rent is only owed at the end of the rental period
steps.whatToRemember: Rent is owed at the end, so a higher rent for paying later is simply the real price. A sale is owed right away, so a higher price for paying later is רבית.

steps.title: רב נחמן: a quiet price increase is allowed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ban on charging 1200 if paid at harvest time. רב נחמן says טרשא, a quiet higher price for later payment, is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'If at the harvest, 1200 זוז, it is forbidden.' רב נחמן said: a quiet price increase is allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה, and רב נחמן adds a ruling that seems to allow something similar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן allows a seller to simply set a higher price with a later payment date. The condition is that he never says the extra is because of the wait. This looks like it clashes with the משנה, which sets up the challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A unit of one hundred zuz
A quiet price increase for delayed payment, without openly saying so

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם לַגּוֹרֶן בִּשְׁנֵים עָשָׂר מָנֶה – אָסוּר.
phrases.english: "And if at the harvest, for twelve hundred, it is forbidden."
phrases.notes: This is a quote from the משנה. The seller openly says: pay now for 1000, or pay at harvest for 1200.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said: A quiet price increase is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם לַגּוֹרֶן בִּשְׁנֵים עָשָׂר מָנֶה – אָסוּר. אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: טַרְשָׁא שְׁרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next line of the משנה and adds an אמורא's ruling
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Setting a higher price for later payment is allowed, as long as the seller does not say the extra is for waiting.

steps.title: Challenge to רב נחמן from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא, or some say רב עוקבא בר חמא, challenges רב נחמן: the משנה forbids 1200 at harvest time!
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא (some say רב עוקבא בר חמא) objected to רב נחמן: the משנה says that 1200 at harvest time is forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: Someone challenges רב נחמן by pointing to the משנה, which seems to forbid exactly what he allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה the buyer also pays more for paying later, and the משנה says this is forbidden. So how can רב נחמן allow a higher price for later payment?

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection to him

phrases.aramaic: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא לְרַב נַחְמָן,
phrases.english: Rami bar Chama objected to Rav Nachman,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רַב עוּקְבָא בַּר חָמָא לְרַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: and some say it was Rav Ukva bar Chama to Rav Nachman:

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם לַגּוֹרֶן בִּשְׁנֵים עָשָׂר מָנֶה – אָסוּר!
phrases.english: "And if at the harvest, for twelve hundred, it is forbidden!"

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא לְרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב נחמן's ruling from step 18
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling that טרשא is permitted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה forbids a higher price for paying at harvest time, which looks just like טרשא.

steps.title: Openly stating the extra charge versus just quoting a price
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that in the משנה the seller openly set the extra as a charge for waiting. In his case, the seller just named one higher price.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: There, he fixed the extra for him as a charge for waiting. Here, he did not.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן defends his ruling by showing his case is different from the משנה's case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה the seller offers two prices: 1000 now or 1200 later. That openly shows the extra 200 is payment for waiting. In טרשא the seller names only one price with a later date and never mentions a cheaper price for paying now, so it is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: He fixed it for him, meaning he openly stated the price difference

steps.confusionAlert: טרשא does not mean any higher price for later payment is fine. It works only when the seller never offers a cheaper price for paying now.

phrases.english: He said to him: There, he fixed it for him;
phrases.notes: In the משנה the seller spelled out both prices, so the extra charge for waiting is out in the open.

phrases.english: here, he did not fix it for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָתָם – קַץ לֵיהּ, הָכָא – לָא קַץ לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 19
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any higher price for later payment is forbidden, as in the משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only an openly stated extra charge for waiting is forbidden. A single quoted higher price is allowed.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה forbids naming two prices, one for now and one for later. טרשא, naming just one higher price with a later date, is allowed.

steps.title: רב פפא: why his delayed-payment beer sales are allowed
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says his own טרשא is allowed. His beer would not spoil and he does not need the money, so selling it early on credit is a favor to the buyer.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: My delayed-payment sales are allowed. Why? My beer would not go bad, and I do not need the money. I am the one doing the buyer a favor.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives his own case of טרשא and explains why it is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא could have held onto his beer and sold it later at the higher price, since it would not spoil and he did not need cash. So he is not being paid for waiting for his money. He is doing the buyer a favor by letting him have the beer now and pay later at the later price.
steps.whyThisMatters: It gives an added reason why a delayed payment at a higher price can be allowed: the seller gains nothing from the wait that he would not have gotten anyway.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: טַרְשָׁא דִּידִי שְׁרֵי,
phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: My quiet price increase is permitted.
What is the reason? My beer does not go bad,
I do not need the money,

phrases.aramaic: אֲנָא הוּא דְּקָא עָבֵידְנָא מִילְּתָא גַּבֵּי לוֹקֵחַ.
phrases.english: it is I who am doing a favor for the buyer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: טַרְשָׁא דִּידִי שְׁרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further case and reason supporting the permission of טרשא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A higher price for delayed payment is allowed when the seller could have waited and sold at that price anyway, so he is doing the buyer a favor.

steps.title: Look at the buyers' side, not the seller's
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת בריה דרב אידי challenges רב פפא. Why judge the deal only from the seller's side? The buyers pay the higher price only because they have no cash now, so they are really paying for time.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת, son of רב אידי, said to רב פפא: Why do you look only at your own side? Look at the buyers' side! If they had money, they would buy at today's price. Now that they have no money, they buy at the later, higher price.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת בריה דרב אידי attacks רב פפא's reason for allowing his טרשא. He says you must also look at it from the buyers' side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא said his deal was fine because he gained nothing from waiting: his beer would not spoil, and he did not need the money. רב ששת answers that the buyers still pay more only because they pay later, so from their side the extra looks like payment for time. The גמרא records no answer from רב פפא.

keyTerms.meaning: What does the Master see? A polite way to ask 'Why do you think so?'
After your own side, judging from your own point of view

steps.confusionAlert: רב ששת is not saying רב פפא gains from waiting. He does not argue with that point at all. His point is that the buyer's side alone can make it look like paying for time.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב שֵׁשֶׁת בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי לְרַב פָּפָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Sheshet, son of Rav Idi, said to Rav Pappa:
What does the Master see
that you go after your own side?
phrases.notes: He means רב פפא's reason from the step before: his beer won't spoil and he doesn't need the cash.

phrases.english: Go after their side,
for if they had money,
they would buy at the current price;
now that they have no money,
they buy at the later, higher price!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב שֵׁשֶׁת בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי לְרַב פָּפָּא: מַאי חָזֵי מָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason רב פפא gave in step 21 for allowing his טרשא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's claim that his טרשא is allowed because he himself gains nothing from waiting.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The buyers pay the higher price only because they cannot pay now. So from their side, the extra is a payment for time, which looks like ריבית.

steps.title: רב חמא says his own טרשא is surely allowed
steps.stepSummary: רב חמא says the טרשא deal he makes is certainly permitted. The next step gives his reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חמא said: My טרשא is certainly permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא, רב חמא, says his own kind of טרשא is surely allowed. This sets up the next step, where his reason is given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא's case was just challenged. רב חמא now brings a case he thinks avoids that problem, so he says 'certainly'. His point will be that the buyers pay more for a real benefit, not for waiting.

phrases.english: Rav Chama said:
My tacit-interest deal is certainly permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חָמָא: טַרְשָׁא דִּידִי וַדַּאי שְׁרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב פפא's case is challenged, a different אמורא brings his own case of טרשא that he says is surely allowed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב חמא's טרשא is certainly permitted.

steps.title: The reason: the buyers gain from his name
steps.stepSummary: Why is רב חמא's deal allowed? The buyers want the goods to stay in his ownership. Wherever they go, they are let off the tax and given a hold on the market. The higher price pays for those benefits.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? It is good for them that the goods stay in my ownership. Wherever they go, people let them off the tax and keep the market for them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רב חמא's deal is allowed, and he gives the reason. The buyers gain real benefits from the goods still being his.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת's challenge was that the buyer pays more only because he pays later. Here the buyer pays more for something else: while the goods are still רב חמא's, they are let off the tax and get a hold on the market. So the extra money is for those benefits, not for waiting.

keyTerms.meaning: It is good for them, they want it

steps.whatToRemember: A higher price for later payment is not ריבית when the extra pays for a real benefit, like tax relief and a hold on the market, rather than for the waiting itself.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
It is good for them that the goods stay in my ownership,
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the buyers. 'The goods' is not in the text; the גמרא assumes it.

phrases.english: for wherever they go,
they let them off the tax
and hold the market for them.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the corrected word is in square brackets. Both mean about the same: 'and they hold.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא – נִיחָא לְהוּ דְּלֵיקוּ בִּרְשׁוּתִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind רב חמא's statement in step 23.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why is רב חמא's טרשא certainly permitted?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The buyers want the goods to stay in his ownership, because then they are let off the tax and get a hold on the market. The higher price pays for that, not for waiting.
